risk_reward.asymmetry_assessment: The distribution IS skewed in our favour, but modestly and for a specific mechanical reason: the upside case is worth 246.5 pips while the downside case is worth only 103.5 pips, because a 0th-percentile leveraged short can cover violently but cannot extend much further. The 25/25 probability weighting therefore understates the payoff asymmetry. The offsetting drag is negative carry of 137.5bp annualised, which converts a 1.13:1 gross ratio into 0.89:1 net over a four-week hold — this is the reason the view is best expressed with a short holding period or through the discounted call wing rather than as a carry-negative spot position held open-endedly.

weighted_score.interpretation: A net score of +0.0820 sits inside the -0.10 to +0.10 Neutral band and is materially weaker than the tactical +0.1876. The arithmetic is a near-standoff: three positive contributions totalling +0.2592 (Policy & Rates +0.1248, Guidance +0.0684, USD Liquidity +0.0660) against three negatives totalling -0.1772 (External Balance -0.1088, Fiscal -0.0399, Event Risk -0.0285), with four factors contributing exactly zero. External Balance alone offsets 87% of the Policy & Rates contribution. This is the numerical expression of the central tension in the dossier: the ECB is hiking BECAUSE the euro area is being taxed by an energy shock, so the rate benefit and the balance-of-payments cost have the same cause and largely cancel. The score is 0.0064 lower than the pre-verification draft of +0.0884 after confidences were reduced on eight factors; the stance is unchanged.
weighted_score.mapping_to_conviction: An absolute score below 0.10 maps to Neutral. We set conviction at 2 of 5 rather than 1 because the offsetting forces are individually large and well-evidenced — a 50bp policy-differential compression against a 30 basis point of GDP erosion in the current account — rather than uniformly weak. Conviction 1 would imply the factors were simply undetermined; they are not, they are opposed. Conviction 3 in either direction would require External Balance to resolve, which means either a Russia-Ukraine settlement or a full Hormuz closure.

strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the dossier is dominated by Policy & Rates at 0.24 and External Balance at 0.16, which together carry 40% of the score and point in opposite directions with almost equal force. Policy & Rates turns Bullish because the trajectory of the differential is euro-favourable for the first time in three years: the ECB has one hike delivered, a 77-83% probability of a second on 10 September and a 91.9% cumulative probability of being above 2.25% by 17 December, while the Fed sits at 3.50-3.75% with a June SEP median implying at most one further increase. If the ECB delivers 50bp and the Fed nothing, the 137.5bp gap compresses to 87.5bp, worth 1.5-2.0 big figures on EUR/USD on the pair's historical beta to the UST-Bund spread. The euro's real policy rate of minus 0.65% against the dollar's plus 0.13% says the ECB has further to travel than the Fed. Guidance & Credibility reinforces this at a 0.12 weight, because Lagarde has published an explicit reaction function, longer-term inflation expectations remain anchored at around 2%, and the June hike was unanimous under every scenario in the projection set. Against that stands the single most serious structural problem the euro has: the current account surplus has narrowed from 2.0% to 1.7% of GDP in twelve months, the goods surplus has fallen from EUR350bn to EUR286bn, the monthly goods balance has flipped to a EUR7.8bn deficit, EU gas storage is roughly 10 percentage points behind last year with the balance-of-summer TTF contract trading EUR2.68/MWh OVER Winter 26/27, and the full EU ban on Russian LNG lands at end-2026. Fiscal & Sovereign Risk compounds it, with the French PLF 2027 solemn vote on 17 November a genuine binary that we estimate at 20-25% risk of a censure-and-dissolution path, and OAT-Bund at 82bp already trading through Italy. The factor interactions are the crux: the rate benefit and the external cost share a single cause, so they cannot both resolve favourably. What is priced is a 2027 consensus of EUR/USD at 1.20-1.22 built on Fed cuts that the 29 July FOMC dissents make unlikely; what we expect is 1.1550 at six months, roughly 50 pips BELOW the 1.1600 forward outright. The path of least resistance is sideways with a widening distribution. Key dated catalysts are 10 September (ECB projections in Berlin), 17 November (French budget), 17 December (ECB projections plus European Council) and end-December (Russian LNG ban). The conviction driver is not direction but the identification of a genuine offsetting structure — this is a Neutral we have argued for, not defaulted to. Actionability is limited in spot and high in volatility: with 3M implied at 5.70 embedding no premium for a dense November-December calendar, the tradeable expression of this view is long volatility and relative value, not a directional euro position.

g10_ranking.commentary: The euro slips from fourth tactically to sixth strategically because the weight migrates from the factors it wins on to the factor it loses on: Inflation & Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and Flows from 0.10 to 0.06, while External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16. Every currency ranked above it has either a large current-account surplus (Norway 15.6%, Singapore 16.7%), a hard carry advantage (Norway 200bp, New Zealand 25bp and rising), or benefits directly from the energy shock damaging the euro. It still beats sterling, whose external position is worse at -2.8% of GDP, and the yen, franc and krona, all of which it out-carries.

strategic.path_expectation: The strategic path is a dispersion trade rather than a level trade. We expect three distinct regimes inside six months. August through mid-September is the tactical squeeze extending to 1.1650-1.1700 as leveraged shorts cover into the Berlin ECB meeting. Mid-September through November is the fade, as the delivered hike becomes a sell-the-fact, the French budget calendar dominates from the 30 September Conseil des ministres through the 20 October and 17 November votes, and European gas storage enters winter roughly 10 percentage points behind; this is where EUR/USD should revisit 1.1450-1.1500 and where realised volatility should rise from 4% toward 6-7%. December through February is the resolution, driven by the 17 December ECB projection round, the 17-18 December European Council on the multiannual financial framework (Council calendar, retrieved 1 August 2026) and the end-2026 Russian LNG ban, with the outcome genuinely two-sided. The shape is a broad W with a widening amplitude, not a grind and not a trend, and the practical implication is that position sizing should shrink into the November-December window even though the central expectation is flat.

Adding the 137.5bp annualised negative carry (roughly 79 pips over six months), a long spot euro position held for six months returns approximately -62 pips net.
risk_reward.downside_case_loss: Downside case EUR/USD 1.1150 versus spot 1.15335 is a loss of approximately 384 pips, or -3.32%, plus 79 pips of negative carry, for a net loss of approximately 463 pips.
risk_reward.risk_reward_ratio: 0.04:1 on the base case alone (17 pips of spot upside against 384 pips of downside), which is another way of saying there is no directional spot trade here. Including the upside case of 1.1850 (+317 pips), the probability-weighted expected value is -9 pips gross (0.50 x 16.5 + 0.25 x 316.5 + 0.25 x -383.5) and roughly -88 pips net of carry.
risk_reward.asymmetry_assessment: The distribution is NOT skewed in our favour and is in fact mildly negative once carry is included, which is precisely why the strategic stance is Neutral and why we do not recommend a directional spot position at this horizon. The genuine asymmetry lies elsewhere: the upside and downside tails are roughly symmetric in magnitude (+317 versus -384 pips) while three-month implied volatility of 5.70 embeds no premium for the November-December event cluster. That is a long-volatility payoff, not a long-euro payoff, and it is the only strategically attractive expression of this dossier.

consensus_divergence.consensus_view: The published consensus is materially more bullish on the euro than we are, and it has unusually low internal agreement. A Bloomberg survey of 23 analysts put EUR/USD averaging 1.20-1.22 across 2026 with a 1.15 low and 1.25 high, and a forecast standard deviation of 4.2 cents — the widest since 2022. Named houses retrieved this cycle: UBS 1.16 for September 2026, 1.18 end-2026 and 1.20 for March and June 2027; Bank of America 1.12 end-Q3 2026, 1.15 end-2026 and 1.20 end-2027; JPMorgan 1.16-1.18 near-term with a 1.20 December 2026 target; Goldman Sachs 1.25 year-end 2026; Deutsche Bank 1.25 end-2026 and a rates view that the ECB goes to 2.50% in September with risk of 2.75%; Morgan Stanley 1.10-1.12 if the energy shock persists; Nordea toward 1.28 in 2027; Citi and Danske Bank as the bearish outliers at 1.12-1.14 [40]. The median of the named set for end-2026 is roughly 1.20. Bank of America's technical desk separately targeted 1.1240 with invalidation above the 23 July high of 1.1436 — a level spot has already exceeded [38].
consensus_divergence.our_view: We expect EUR/USD at 1.1650 in one month, 1.1600 in three months and 1.1550 in six months. Tactically that is more bullish than Bank of America and Morgan Stanley and broadly in line with UBS; strategically it is 250-450 pips BELOW the 1.18-1.22 cluster that constitutes the mainstream view. We are bullish where the consensus is bearish (the next four weeks) and neutral-to-bearish where the consensus is bullish (the next six months).
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Approximately 450 pips, or 3.9%, against the Bloomberg 1.20 lower bound for 2026, and approximately 250 pips against UBS's 1.18 end-2026 forecast. Against Goldman Sachs and Deutsche Bank at 1.25 the divergence widens to roughly 950 pips, or 8.2%. In the other direction we are approximately 400 pips ABOVE Morgan Stanley's 1.10-1.12 energy-shock scenario and 310 pips above Bank of America's 1.1240 technical target.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Three specific analytical differences. First, the transmission assumption. Almost every forecast in the 1.20-1.25 cluster is built on the sequence 'Fed cuts, differential compresses, dollar falls, euro absorbs it'. The 29 July FOMC held 9-3 with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting in favour of a HIKE, and the June SEP median for end-2026 is 3.8% against a 3.625% midpoint [39]. The compression that arrives will come from the euro leg alone, which halves its magnitude. Second, the market underweights External Balance. The consensus reads the ECB's hiking cycle as a euro positive and stops there; it does not net the same shock's cost, which is a current-account surplus falling from 2.0% to 1.7% of GDP, a monthly goods balance swinging EUR22.8bn into deficit year-on-year, and EU gas storage roughly 10 percentage points behind entering a winter that also carries a self-imposed Russian LNG ban [16][17][33][34]. The rate benefit and the external cost share one cause and largely cancel; the consensus counts only the benefit. Third, the market has not dated the French binary. The PLF 2027 solemn vote on 17 November is not visible in the OAT forward curve or in EUR/USD option expiries, and we put a 20-25% probability on a censure-and-dissolution path that would take OAT-Bund through 130bp weeks before a presidential campaign in which Bardella polls at 35%. The dispersion in the consensus itself — a 4.2-cent standard deviation, the widest since 2022 — is evidence that the market knows it cannot resolve these forces and has averaged them instead.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: A six-month EUR/USD forward sale at the 1.1600 outright against an expected 1.1550 earns approximately 50 pips, or 0.43%, which is a small absolute payoff and honestly reflects a Neutral strategic stance. The larger payoff is in volatility and relative value: three-month implied at 5.70 embeds no premium for the 17 November French vote, the 17 December ECB projection round or the end-2026 Russian LNG ban, so long three-to-six-month volatility is the asymmetric expression. On the tactical side, being long the euro from 1.15335 into a 1.1650 target while consensus technical desks target 1.1240 earns approximately 117 pips against a crowd positioned the other way.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If the consensus is right and EUR/USD reaches 1.20 by end-2026, a six-month forward sale from 1.1600 loses approximately 400 pips, or 3.4%, and a long-volatility position would still profit from the realised move, which is the practical reason to prefer the volatility expression. The specific scenarios that make consensus right are a Russia-Ukraine settlement collapsing the energy premium and a deterioration in US payrolls that converts the FOMC's hawkish dissenters into a cutting majority. We assign those a combined probability of roughly 25%, which is exactly the weight on our upside case.

cleanest_bullish_expression.rationale: The cleanest long-euro expression available. It carries the largest positive carry the euro enjoys anywhere at 225bp, widening to 250bp if the ECB hikes on 10 September, against an SNB whose own conditional forecast assumes a 0.00% policy rate across the entire horizon with inflation at 0.6%. The Bund yields 268bp more than the 10Y Swiss Confederation bond, the widest positive spread in the set. Cross volatility is the lowest in the complex at an estimated 4.5, giving the best carry-to-vol ratio available to a euro long at approximately +0.50, and a carry-collecting long can absorb a 1.1% adverse move over six months before losing money. Valuation is neutral — the euro is only 0.6% rich against the franc on relative REER deviation — so nothing in the valuation channel opposes the trade. It is also the expression that best isolates the euro's improving policy trajectory from its deteriorating external balance, because Switzerland shares the euro area's energy-importer status and therefore nets out the terms-of-trade shock. The pair is already up 1.14% on the month and 1.68% over six months, so the carry is working.

cleanest_bearish_expression.rationale: If the euro view is wrong, this is where it breaks first and hardest, and it is therefore the cleanest short-euro expression. Norway out-carries the euro area by 200bp with Norges Bank's own published forecast pointing to just above 4.5% by year-end and a live meeting on 13 August; the euro area is a net energy importer while Norway is the G10's largest energy exporter with a 15.6% of GDP current-account surplus against the euro area's 1.7%. The same Brent move from $79 to $90.24 and the same TTF surge to EUR58.62/MWh that taxes the euro directly funds the krone. The cross has already fallen 3.06% in a month and 7.25% over twelve months, so the trend is established rather than speculative. The offset, and it is why this is a relative-value idea rather than an outright recommendation, is that the krone's REER is 5.5% above its 30-month mean, the second most stretched in the set, so 5.0% of the euro's cheapness against the krone on relative REER is a genuine brake.

relative_value_pairs.thesis: This pair isolates the central claim of the dossier — that the euro's improving carry is real but its terms of trade are deteriorating — and hedges out the dollar leg entirely. The long EUR/CHF side collects 225bp rising to 250bp against a central bank that cannot move; the short EUR/NOK side sells the euro against the currency that most directly benefits from the energy shock. If our tactical Bullish and strategic Neutral combination is right, both legs work: the euro rises against the zero-yielder and falls against the energy exporter. The pair fails only if the energy shock reverses entirely, in which case EUR/NOK rallies hard while EUR/CHF is unaffected.

The purest test of relative fundamentals in the set, because policy rates are EXACTLY level at 2.25% and carry is therefore precisely zero. Every basis point of ECB tightening from 10 September creates a carry advantage from a standing start — a 50bp swing by year-end is the largest available change in relative carry anywhere in the G10+SGD complex. Fundamentally the ECB is hiking into 2.9% inflation while the Bank of Canada faces CPI-trim at 1.8%, CPI-median at 1.9% and unemployment at 6.5%, with Canadian GDP contracting 0.05% year-on-year and a 50% US Section 338 tariff landing around 19 August. The cross at 1.61690 is flat on the month and up 2.26% on the year.

A relative-value idea in volatility rather than direction. Both the ECB and the BoJ are tightening, and the Bund-JGB spread has compressed to just 37bp with JGB yields up 122bp year-on-year, which means the cross's traditional carry anchor is eroding fast. EUR/JPY is up 6.26% on the year on a differential that is narrowing, and suspected Japanese intervention around USD/JPY 157-158 with 1M risk reversals showing a 1.5-vol premium for yen calls indicates official sensitivity. That combination — an eroding fundamental anchor and an official reaction function — usually resolves in higher realised volatility regardless of direction.

cross_horizon_consistency.summary: The horizons are NOT aligned: tactically Bullish at conviction 2 with a weighted score of +0.1876, strategically Neutral at conviction 2 with +0.0820. The stance difference is genuine and mechanical, not a hedge.
cross_horizon_consistency.divergence_explanation: The divergence is created almost entirely by the weight migration between horizons. Inflation & Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and Flows & Positioning from 0.10 to 0.06 — those are the two factors contributing +0.1080 and +0.0620 tactically, and together they lose 0.12 of weight. External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16 and Fiscal & Sovereign Risk from 0.04 to 0.07, and those are the two largest negatives. Policy & Rates, weighted 0.24 on both horizons, switches from Neutral to Bullish and adds +0.1248, which partly compensates, but not enough. Substantively the story is that the tactical case rests on two things with short half-lives — a July data cluster that surprised hawkishly and a 0th-percentile leveraged short — while the strategic case must contend with an energy import bill and a French budget calendar that only get heavier with time.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Mid-to-late September 2026, specifically the window between the 10 September ECB decision in Berlin and the 30 September French Conseil des ministres. The 10 September meeting is the point at which the tactical thesis is either delivered or invalidated; a delivered hike with 77-83% already priced is a classic sell-the-fact, and the leveraged short that powers the squeeze will by then have been substantially covered. From 30 September the French budget calendar takes over as the dominant euro-specific narrative, and European gas storage enters the final month of the injection season roughly 10 percentage points behind.
cross_horizon_consistency.catalyst_for_transition: The 10 September ECB decision and staff projections, followed by the 30 September tabling of the PLF 2027 and PLFSS 2027 in the French Conseil des ministres. The first exhausts the tactical catalyst set; the second opens the strategic risk set. A secondary transition marker is the 1 November EU gas storage reading — if it is below 75%, the External Balance factor moves from Bearish 70 toward Bearish 80 and the strategic score turns negative.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Because the horizons disagree, the position must be time-boxed rather than held open-endedly. The tactical long should be sized for a two-to-four-week hold with a hard invalidation at 1.1470 and should be reduced into rather than held through the 10 September decision, since the negative carry of 137.5bp annualised makes an open-ended long expensive. The strategic view is not a spot view at all: with a probability-weighted expected value of -9 pips gross and -88 pips net of carry, there is no directional trade, and the exploitable strategic position is long three-to-six-month volatility, where the market charges nothing for the November-December event cluster. In relative-value terms, long EUR/CHF works on both horizons while long EUR/USD works on only one.

forward_vs_spot.interpretation: The forward curve prices the euro to appreciate 1.15-1.49% annualised purely as a function of the 137.5bp negative carry, with the premium declining across tenors as the curve embeds ECB tightening. That declining premium is the market already agreeing with our strategic Policy & Rates thesis — the convergence trade is not a fresh idea, it is in the price. The exploitable observation is that the shape of our expected path differs from the shape of the forward path: the forwards imply a monotonic drift higher, whereas we expect a spike to 1.1650 by early September and then a fade back to 1.1550 by February. That is a term-structure trade rather than a level trade, and it is why the combined tactical-long, strategic-forward-short position is internally coherent rather than contradictory: we are long the front of our own expected path and short the back of the market's.

key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD; the single highest-beta US release for the pair.

key_catalysts.rationale: Norges Bank held at 4.25% in June but the Governor said explicitly that the rate will be raised at one of the forthcoming meetings if developments proceed as envisaged, and the published forecast points to just above 4.5% by year-end. A hike widens the euro's carry deficit to 225bp against a currency already benefiting from the same energy shock that taxes the euro.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — the market prices a hike by year-end but is split on August versus September.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/NOK above all — the euro's weakest cross, down 7.25% over twelve months.

key_catalysts.event: Eurostat euro-area GDP, Q2 2026 t+45 flash estimate
key_catalysts.rationale: The 30 July preliminary flash of +0.4% quarter-on-quarter beat a 0.2% consensus and covered 19 member states representing 96% of euro-area GDP. The t+45 estimate adds the remainder and the first expenditure breakdown. A downward revision to 0.2% would remove the strongest single pillar of the tactical bull case.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — revisions to euro-area flash GDP are rarely traded, which is precisely why a revision would move the market.

key_catalysts.event: Publication of the ECB Account of the 23 July 2026 monetary policy meeting
key_catalysts.rationale: Lagarde disclosed at the press conference that some governors asked whether a hike should be considered, and the Account will document how many and how forcefully. Given that the June Account recorded a unanimous hike and an all-member view that inflation risks are to the upside, a hawkish July Account would push September pricing from 77-83% toward 90%.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — the direction is known, the intensity is not. The June Account's disclosure that markets priced an 84% chance of a THIRD hike by end-2026 sets a hawkish benchmark.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD, EUR/CHF and EUR/JPY through the rate-expectations channel.

key_catalysts.event: Fitch scheduled sovereign rating review of France
key_catalysts.rationale: Fitch downgraded France to A+ in September 2025 and currently carries a Stable outlook. With the 2025 deficit at 5.1% of GDP, debt at 117.5% and a Bercy-commissioned report warning of 5.9% in 2027, an outlook change to Negative is a live possibility ahead of the PLF 2027 process. It would take OAT-Bund from 82bp toward 95-100bp.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — the OAT forward curve carries no visible premium around the date.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD and EUR/CHF; peripheral stress is a euro-wide event, not a French one.

key_catalysts.event: Eurostat euro-area flash HICP for August 2026 and euro-area unemployment for July 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: This is the decisive input for the 10 September ECB decision. July printed 2.9% headline, 2.5% core, 3.3% services and 10.0% energy, all accelerating. We expect 2.9-3.1% headline. A print at or above 2.9% locks in the September hike; a print at or below 2.6% cuts hike odds below 55% and invalidates the tactical thesis.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — the market prices continuation at 2.8-3.0% but is not positioned for an upside surprise, given a 0th-percentile leveraged short.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/SEK — every cross where the euro's rate trajectory is the swing variable.

key_catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision plus ECB staff macroeconomic projections, hosted by the Bundesbank in Berlin
key_catalysts.rationale: The single most important dated event in this dossier. A 25bp hike to 2.50% is 77-83% priced, but the projections carry the larger information content: the June round had HICP peaking at 3.4% in Q3-Q4 2026 with 2027 at 2.3% and embedded almost three hikes. An upward revision to 2026 inflation toward 3.2% with 2027 held at or above 2.3% forces the curve higher; a downward revision to 2027 caps the cycle at 2.50%.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully for the hike itself at 77-83%; not at all for the projection revisions. This is a classic sell-the-fact risk on the rate and a genuine two-sided risk on the projections.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All euro crosses; most acute for EUR/CHF, where a hike widens carry to 250bp against a static SNB.

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision plus Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The dollar leg of the differential. The 29 July hold was 9-3 with all three dissents favouring a HIKE, and the June SEP median for end-2026 is 3.8%. If the September SEP retains that median, the differential compression on which the strategic Policy & Rates stance rests is halved.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — the market prices a hold but has not resolved whether the dissenters become a majority.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD; the pair's dominant driver alongside the ECB.

key_catalysts.event: German state elections in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin
key_catalysts.rationale: The highest-salience German political event of the autumn, with the AfD polling ahead in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. A strong AfD result would pressure the Merz CDU/CSU-SPD coalition at exactly the moment it is passing a 2027 draft budget carrying EUR109.7bn of defence spending, raising questions about the durability of the German fiscal expansion that underpins Bund yields.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — no measurable premium in Bund futures or EUR/USD options.

key_catalysts.event: Google 60-day Digital Markets Act compliance deadline following the ~USD1bn fine of 23 July 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: Non-compliance triggers penalties of up to 5% of daily turnover and is the single most likely trigger for the Section 301 action President Trump threatened on 24-25 July over EU fines on US technology firms. The 15% EU tariff ceiling in force since 1 July is politically rather than legally secure, and both sides hold unilateral suspension levers.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. Exact date is derived from the 23 July fine plus 60 days and is stated in YYYY-MM-WN form because no official deadline date was published.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD; secondarily EUR/SEK and EUR/NOK through European equity beta.

key_catalysts.event: French PLF 2027 and PLFSS 2027 presented to the Conseil des ministres
key_catalysts.rationale: The formal opening of the French budget process and the start of the euro's dominant autumn risk. The government's July framework caps ministry spending growth at 0.4%, roughly four times slower than inflation, while debt interest rises EUR12.3bn and defence rises EUR6.4bn. The 2026 budget required Article 49.3 and survived censure motions; the 2027 budget is the last of Macron's term.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — OAT-Bund at 82bp carries no event premium for the autumn sequence.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD and EUR/CHF; historically an OAT-Bund move through 100bp drags EUR/USD 1.0-1.5% lower.

key_catalysts.event: EU Draft Budgetary Plans for 2027 due; European Council meets 15-16 October in Brussels
key_catalysts.rationale: The first hard, comparable read on France's and Italy's 2027 fiscal stance, alongside a European Council that addresses the 2028-34 multiannual financial framework, Ukraine funding and the frozen-asset question the June Council deferred (European Council dates are as published on the Council's meetings calendar at https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/calendar/, retrieved 1 August 2026). A France DBP showing a 2027 deficit above 5.5% would put the Commission on a collision course before the November votes.

key_catalysts.event: Moody's scheduled sovereign rating review of France
key_catalysts.rationale: France is Moody's Aa3 with a NEGATIVE outlook set on 24 October 2025 and reaffirmed 10 April 2026. This review falls three days after the 20 October solemn vote on Part I of the PLF 2027, which gives Moody's a fresh read on political capacity to consolidate. A downgrade to A1 would be the fourth agency action in thirteen months.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — a negative outlook is standing but the review date is not visible in OAT pricing.

key_catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision (Frankfurt, no staff projections)
key_catalysts.rationale: The market assigns an 85.1% cumulative probability that the deposit rate is above 2.25% by this meeting. Without projections the meeting is a pure communication event, and its function will be to signal whether December is live. A hawkish hold that keeps December priced above 60% sustains the euro's rate trajectory.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — cumulative pricing exists but the meeting-specific probability does not.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All euro crosses, most acutely EUR/CHF and EUR/CAD where the ECB is the only moving part.

key_catalysts.event: French Assemblee nationale solemn vote on the PLF 2027 as a whole
key_catalysts.rationale: The peak risk date of the European autumn and the largest identified binary for the euro in this dossier. If Article 49.3 is used without a pre-negotiated compromise, a censure motion follows; a successful censure means dissolution and snap legislative elections weeks before a presidential campaign in which Jordan Bardella polls at 35% against Edouard Philippe at 20.5%. We put the censure-and-dissolution path at 20-25%, taking OAT-Bund from 82bp toward 130bp.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced at all — the date appears in neither the OAT forward curve nor EUR/USD option expiries.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP — a French fiscal event is a euro-wide event.

key_catalysts.event: ECB decision plus Eurosystem staff projections; European Council 17-18 December on the 2028-34 multiannual financial framework
key_catalysts.rationale: A triple-header: the market prices a 91.9% cumulative probability of a deposit rate above 2.25% by this date, the projection round is the first to extend meaningfully into 2029, and leaders have targeted MFF agreement before the end of 2026. The Bank of England and Norges Bank also decide on the same day.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially for the rate at 91.9% cumulative; not at all for the MFF outcome.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All euro crosses; EUR/GBP and EUR/NOK doubly so given the same-day decisions.

key_catalysts.event: Full EU ban on Russian LNG imports takes effect under Regulation (EU) 2026/261
key_catalysts.rationale: A self-imposed supply cut landing in the same month as constrained Hormuz LNG transit and EU storage that entered winter roughly 10 percentage points behind the prior year. Kpler's base case has global LNG exports revised down 21Mt for July 2026 to March 2027, with recovery only in Q1 2027. The euro area's terms of trade take a third simultaneous hit.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — the December TTF strip reflects the ban but not its interaction with a constrained Hormuz and low storage.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/NOK above all; then EUR/USD through the current-account channel.

invalidators.condition: Euro-area flash HICP for August 2026, released 1 September, prints at or below 2.6% year-on-year with core at or below 2.3%
invalidators.mechanism: A sub-2.6% headline with decelerating core would remove the evidentiary basis for a September hike and cut market-implied odds from 77-83% to below 55%. Factor 2 would move from Bullish 60 to Neutral, removing +0.1080 from the tactical score and taking it from +0.1876 to +0.0796, inside the Neutral band. The leveraged short would stop covering and re-build.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Eurostat euro-area flash HICP, headline and HICPX (excluding energy, food, alcohol and tobacco)
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Monthly, on or about the first business day
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Headline at or below 2.6% AND core at or below 2.3%

invalidators.condition: EUR/USD closes below 1.1470 on a daily basis
invalidators.mechanism: 1.1470 is the base of the 30-31 July breakout. A close below it frames the July advance as a post-Fed positioning adjustment rather than a repricing, and opens 1.1436 and then the 1.1336 retracement floor. Because the tactical thesis rests on the breakout holding while shorts cover, the structural invalidation and the flow invalidation are the same level.

invalidators.condition: The ECB holds all three rates unchanged on 10 September 2026 while revising 2027 HICP down to 2.1% or below
invalidators.mechanism: A hold against 77-83% pricing is a 20-25bp dovish repricing on impact, and a 2027 inflation revision below 2.2% would cap the cycle at 2.25% entirely. Factor 1 would move from Neutral to Bearish tactically and from Bullish 55 to Bearish strategically, swinging the strategic score by roughly 0.26 and taking it decisively negative.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ECB Governing Council decision and ECB staff macroeconomic projections
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Deposit rate unchanged at 2.25% AND 2027 HICP projection at or below 2.1%

invalidators.condition: Dutch TTF front-month gas sustains above EUR75/MWh for two consecutive weeks with EU storage below 70% on 1 November
invalidators.mechanism: TTF above EUR75 with storage below 70% converts the energy story from an inflation trade the ECB responds to into a euro-area growth and balance-of-payments shock. Factor 5 would move from Bearish 68 to Bearish 85, taking the strategic score from +0.0820 to +0.0548, and Factor 2 would turn Bearish as demand destruction dominates, taking it decisively negative. The current-account surplus would fall below 1.2% of GDP.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ICE Dutch TTF front-month settlement and GIE AGSI EU storage fill percentage
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily for TTF, weekly for storage
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: TTF above EUR75/MWh for ten consecutive business days AND storage below 70% on 1 November 2026

invalidators.condition: A censure motion against the French government succeeds on or around the 17 November PLF 2027 solemn vote, triggering dissolution
invalidators.mechanism: Dissolution weeks before a presidential campaign in which Bardella polls at 35% would take OAT-Bund from 82bp through 130bp and revive the redenomination premium that the Transmission Protection Instrument has never been tested against. Factor 8 would move from Bearish 57 to Bearish 85 and Factor 7 from Bearish 57 to Bearish 75, taking the strategic score to roughly +0.0437 and then negative as Factor 3 follows. Historically an OAT-Bund move through 100bp drags EUR/USD 1.0-1.5% lower independent of the ECB.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: French Assemblee nationale censure motion votes and the OAT-Bund 10Y spread
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily for the spread; per vote for the motions
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: A censure motion carrying an absolute majority of 289 votes, or OAT-Bund closing above 110bp

invalidators.condition: The UST-Bund 10Y spread compresses below 130bp with the ECB having delivered at least one further hike
invalidators.mechanism: This is the bullish invalidator. A move from 159bp to below 130bp is 29bp of compression, worth roughly 1.0-1.3 big figures on EUR/USD on the pair's historical beta, and it would confirm that the euro leg is doing the work rather than requiring Fed cuts. Factor 1 would move from Bullish 52 to Bullish 70, taking the strategic score from +0.0820 to +0.1180 and out of the Neutral band.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: US 10Y Treasury yield minus German 10Y Bund yield
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Spread below 130bp on a five-day average AND ECB deposit rate at or above 2.50%

invalidators.condition: CFTC leveraged funds flip from net short 56,671 contracts to net long more than 25,000 contracts
invalidators.mechanism: An 82,000-contract swing would completely exhaust the contrarian support underpinning the tactical view. Factor 4 would move from Bullish 62 to Neutral, removing +0.0620 from the tactical score and taking it from +0.1876 to +0.1256 — still Bullish but at the bottom of the conviction-2 band, and with the squeeze fuel spent.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC Commitments of Traders, EURO FX, leveraged funds net position
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Weekly, Friday afternoon, for the prior Tuesday
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Leveraged funds net long more than 25,000 contracts

invalidators.condition: The euro-area twelve-month current account surplus recovers above 2.0% of GDP in the monthly ECB balance of payments release
invalidators.mechanism: A recovery from 1.7% to above 2.0% would mean the energy shock has been absorbed without permanent damage to the external position. Factor 5 would move from Bearish 68 to Neutral, removing -0.1088 from the strategic score and taking it from +0.0820 to +0.1908, decisively Bullish and out of the Neutral band. This is the single largest available swing factor in the strategic score.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ECB monthly euro area balance of payments, twelve-month cumulated current account as a percentage of GDP
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Monthly, roughly seven weeks after the reference month
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Twelve-month cumulated surplus above 2.0% of GDP

factors_changed.reason: The July dossier read the 137.5bp Fed premium and a hawkish Warsh FOMC as decisively euro-negative. A month later the level is unchanged but the trajectory has flipped: the 29 July FOMC held 9-3 with all three dissents favouring a HIKE rather than a cut, while ECB September hike pricing rose to 77-83% and the cumulative probability of a higher deposit rate by 17 December reached 91.9%. Tactically the hike is now fully priced so the factor generates no signal; strategically the compression is real and comes from the euro leg.

July delivered a hawkish data cluster the prior report could not have seen: flash HICP accelerated on all four components (headline 2.9%, core 2.5%, services 3.3%, energy 10.0%), Q2 GDP beat at +0.4% q/q against a 0.2% consensus, and the composite PMI rose to a five-month high of 51.9 from the 49.5 recorded in the prior dossier. Strategically unchanged, because the wage tracker at 2.3% still shows no second-round effects.

Downgraded tactically. European equities have gone on to record highs — the STOXX Europe 600 at 655.45 — yet the euro captured only 1.36% of that in July, a realised beta well under one. The prior report's expectation that a risk-on regime would carry the euro has been tested and largely failed, because the euro's funding-currency drag offsets the anti-dollar bid.

The single largest tactical reversal in the dossier. Leveraged funds sold 41,261 EURO FX contracts over four weeks to reach net short 56,671 — the 0th percentile of the 25-week range. What was a bearish momentum signal a month ago is now a contrarian squeeze setup in the largest CME FX contract by open interest. The strategic reading is unchanged because the asset-manager long of 228,927 is the slow-moving overhang either way.

The most consequential change in the report and a complete reversal. The July dossier was built on the Islamabad Memorandum reopening the Strait of Hormuz and WTI collapsing to roughly $70.5 — a terms-of-trade relief. That relief has been entirely undone: the ceasefire collapsed, Brent rose 24-26% in July to $90.24, TTF gas is EUR58.62/MWh and up 66% year-on-year, the goods balance swung EUR22.8bn into deficit year-on-year, and the twelve-month current-account surplus fell from 2.0% to 1.7% of GDP. At a 0.16 strategic weight this reversal alone costs the strategic score roughly 0.21.

Upgraded on documented evidence rather than interpretation. Lagarde described the Sintra 'more balanced risks' formulation as removed at the 23 July meeting (FLAGGED — press-conference-sourced only) and disclosed internal pressure for a hike, the June Account showed a unanimous decision justified under every projection scenario, and Schnabel stated publicly that rates 'are not yet restrictive' and that further increases will be needed.

Downgraded because the prior report's central geopolitical assumption — Hormuz reopened under the Islamabad Memorandum — has been invalidated. The ceasefire collapsed, US strikes resumed, the Houthis imposed a Red Sea blockade, Iranian forces interdicted tankers on 30-31 July, and a new transatlantic vector opened with the Section 301 threat over EU technology fines on 24-25 July.

Downgraded as the French budget calendar entered the strategic window. The OAT reached a 17-year high twice in July and OAT-Bund at 81-82bp now trades at or THROUGH the BTP-Bund spread of 80-81bp — an inversion of the euro area's historical credit hierarchy. The PLF 2027 sequence (30 September, 20 October, 17 November) plus four French rating reviews between 28 August and 27 November are all new to this horizon.

Upgraded tactically because the structural picture the prior report described has changed: the 1.1330 support the July dossier flagged as the bear trigger held, and EUR/USD reclaimed 1.1500 on 30-31 July. The regime is now range-bound with an upward inflection rather than a bearish grind.

Upgraded on the recognition that the Federal Reserve's balance sheet is EXPANDING — USD6,738.19bn on 29 July against USD6,646.34bn in March — meaning QT has ended as a global dollar drain. Combined with a stable SOFR at 3.65%, IG credit at 81bp and a broad dollar index that fell over the month, the dollar-scarcity premium that supported the currency through 2024-25 has been removed.

conviction_change.explanation: Tactical conviction is unchanged at 2 but the STANCE has flipped from Bearish to Bullish, and the weighted score has swung 0.3716 from -0.1840 to +0.1876 — the largest single-month reversal in the EUR series. Conviction stays at 2 rather than rising to 3 because the two factors driving the flip, a July data cluster and a positioning extreme, both have short half-lives and because the heaviest factor at tactical weights contributes exactly zero. Strategic conviction FALLS from 3 to 2 even though the score is nearly unchanged (+0.0960 to +0.0820), because the composition has deteriorated: a month ago the Neutral was a balance of mostly mild readings, whereas now it is a standoff between a strongly Bullish Policy & Rates (+0.1248) and a strongly Bearish External Balance (-0.1088). A Neutral produced by two large opposing forces is less reliable than a Neutral produced by small ones, and it carries a wider outcome distribution, so conviction is reduced.

change_since_last_report.thesis_trajectory: Reversing tactically, unchanged but more fragile strategically. The thesis is that the euro's tactical position has improved decisively since 1 July 2026 — the prior report's own invalidation condition (1.1330 holds and 1.1500 is reclaimed) was met in full, the composite PMI cleared 50, and leveraged positioning swung to a sample extreme that now works for the euro rather than against it. The strategic thesis is unchanged in level at +0.0820 versus +0.0960 but materially different in composition, because the terms-of-trade relief that underpinned the July report's Bullish External Balance stance has completely reversed and is now the largest single negative in the dossier. Net: the euro is a better two-to-four-week trade and a worse one-to-six-month hold than it was a month ago.

seasonality.pattern: Two documented seasonal patterns are relevant. First, the euro brief identifies June and December ECB forecast revisions as a recurring euro-area seasonal: the Eurosystem staff projection rounds in June and December carry more weight than the March and September ECB staff rounds because they extend the forecast horizon and are produced with national central bank input. Second, and larger this year, European natural gas has a hard physical seasonal turn: the injection season ends on or about 1 November and the withdrawal season begins, at which point the storage level becomes a fixed constraint rather than a variable one. Layered on both is the standard 31 December year-end dollar funding turn, which typically widens cross-currency basis and produces a temporary euro headwind.
seasonality.relevance_window: All three sit inside the strategic horizon. The 1 November storage reading falls at the midpoint, the 17 December Eurosystem staff projection round and the 17-18 December European Council fall in the final month, and the year-end funding turn falls immediately after. None is inside the tactical two-to-four-week window, which is one reason the tactical and strategic assessments diverge.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: Not quantified this cycle. No historical distribution of euro returns around December projection rounds or around the 1 November storage turn was retrievable, and we decline to assert a magnitude we have not measured. The directional logic is sound and the dates are certain; the size is not established and this is flagged as a gap.
seasonality.current_alignment: Aligned with the strategic Bearish stance on Factor 5 (External Balance) and with the Bearish stance on Factor 8 (Fiscal), and mildly opposed to the Bullish strategic stance on Factor 10 (USD Liquidity), since the year-end funding turn is the one predictable moment at which abundant dollar liquidity temporarily tightens. The net seasonal skew over the strategic horizon is euro-negative and concentrated in November and December.

The BIS REER 'historical percentile' of approximately 55 is an estimate. The cached BIS series carries only 30 monthly observations, so the deviation column is a 30-MONTH mean and cannot support a decade-length percentile or be presented as a long-run purchasing-power anchor.

The PPP deviation table is constructed as the difference between the euro area's REER deviation from its 30-month mean (+0.5%) and each peer's equivalent deviation. This is a relative real-effective-valuation method, not an absolute purchasing-power-parity calculation, and the implied fair values follow mechanically from it.
